items.title: Bronx EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought
items.desc:
The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a “Developer” for purposes of developing a parking structure with at least 900 spaces that directly or indirectly benefits Veterans.

 For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the parking structure. 

 VA’s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans, which may include certain parking structures. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA’s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program.

 The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the James J. Peters VAMC Campus under VA’s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. The James J. Peters VAMC is particularly interested in a parking EUL to alleviate the significant on-campus parking shortage.

 Analyze and evaluate plans, programs, and budgets in relation to U.S. defense objectives, projected threats, allied contributions, estimated costs, and resource constraints.

items.title: Baccalaureate Alumni Survey, printing and mailing
items.snippet: NC State University has administered the Baccalaureate Alumni Survey every three years since 2003. The survey provides a unique opportunity to collect information from our recent alumni (graduating 2.5 to 4.5 years prior to the administration of the survey) on
items.desc:
NC State University has administered the Baccalaureate Alumni Survey every three years since 2003. The survey provides a unique opportunity to collect information from our recent alumni (graduating 2.5 to 4.5 years prior to the administration of the survey) on a wide range of topics, including their employment; further education; the outcomes of their participation in high impact experiences; the extent to which NC State helped them develop a wide range of academic, professional and personal skills; and more. Survey results provide important data for planning and assessment activities across campus and are used as metrics in the University Strategic Plan. 
The project uses a “push-to-web” research design, with a series of letters, postcards, and emails sent to members of the survey population, providing them with a link and login credentials to access an online survey. 
The project involves printing, stuffing, stamping and mailing 3 separate mailings. The selected vendor will not be responsible for the administration of the actual survey, which will be done in-house by NC State University. See specifications in the RFQ document.

items.desc:
Lenoir County, North Carolina, is soliciting sealed proposals from qualified firms to provide comprehensive grant administration and construction management services to support a Community Project Funding (CPF) project funded by the Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The County has been awarded $5,182,000 in HUD Economic Development Initiative (EDI) CPF funds, contingent upon execution of the Grant Agreement and satisfaction of all grant conditions.

The selected firm will assist the County with grant administration and construction management services of the CPF project in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including HUD CDBG requirements, 2 CFR Part 200 procurement, and grant management requirements, applicable civil rights and labor standards requirements, and HUD EDI program requirements.
This RFP is intended to comply with the competitive proposal requirements applicable to procurement of grant administration and construction management services under federal grant rules and HUD CPF monitoring expectations.

Project Background
The EDI CPF program is administered by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development and funded through directed Congressional appropriation.
